questions.question: If a side of a square is increased by 20%, then its area will increase by:
questions.questionHtml: If a side of a square is increased by 20%, then its area will increase by:
questions.solution:
Side = a
New side = 1.2a
Old area = a²
New area = (1.2a)² = 1.44a²
Increase = 1.44a² − a² = 0.44a²

Percentage increase = (0.44a² / a²) × 100 = 44%.

questions.question: Suppose M denotes the mean proportional between 16 and 25 and N denotes the third proportional between 9 and 15. Find the value of 4M + 3N.
questions.questionHtml: Suppose M denotes the mean proportional between 16 and 25 and N denotes the third proportional between 9 and 15. Find the value of 4M + 3N.
questions.solution:
Mean proportional between 16 and 25 = √(16 × 25) = √400 = 20
So, M = 20

Third proportional between 9 and 15 →
If a : b :: b : c, then c = b² / a
So, N = (15²) / 9 = 225 / 9 = 25

Now, 4M + 3N = (4 × 20) + (3 × 25) = 80 + 75 = 155

questions.question: If x − y + z : y − z + 2w : 2x + z − w = 2 : 3 : 5, find 3x + 3z − 2w : w.
questions.questionHtml: If x − y + z : y − z + 2w : 2x + z − w = 2 : 3 : 5, find 3x + 3z − 2w : w.
questions.solution:
Given:
x − y + z : y − z + 2w : 2x + z − w = 2 : 3 : 5

Now,
(2 + 3 = 5) means — the third term (2x + z − w) is the sum of the first two (x − y + z) + (y − z + 2w).

So,
x − y + z + y − z + 2w = 2x + z − w
⇒ x + z + 2w = 2x + z − w
⇒ x + z = 3w

Now we need 3x + 3z − 2w : w
Substitute x + z = 3w ⇒

3x + 3z − 2w = 3(x + z) − 2w = 3(3w) − 2w = 9w − 2w = 7w

So, ratio = 7 : 1

questions.question: Find the number which, when successively divided by 3, 5, and 7, leaves remainders 2, 1, and 3 respectively, and the last quotient is 3.
questions.questionHtml: Find the number which, when successively divided by 3, 5, and 7, leaves remainders 2, 1, and 3 respectively, and the last quotient is 3.
questions.solution:
Let the required number be N.

We start backwards (successive division means reverse working):

When divided by 7,
→ Remainder = 3
→ Quotient = 3

So,
Dividend = 7 × 3 + 3 = 24

Now, this 24 was the quotient when N was divided by 5,
→ Remainder = 1

So,
Dividend = 5 × 24 + 1 = 121

Now, this 121 was the quotient when N was divided by 3,
→ Remainder = 2

So,
Dividend = 3 × 121 + 2 = 365

questions.question: Anam and Bikash invest in a business in the ratio 3 : 2. If in a particular month, Anam gets ₹5,121 as profit, the total profit is:
questions.questionHtml: Anam and Bikash invest in a business in the ratio 3 : 2. If in a particular month, Anam gets ₹5,121 as profit, the total profit is:
questions.solution:
Investment ratio of Anam : Bikash = 3 : 2
→ Total parts = 3 + 2 = 5 parts

Anam’s share = 3 parts = ₹5,121

So, value of 1 part = 5121 ÷ 3 = ₹1,707

Total profit = 5 parts = 5 × 1,707 = ₹8,535

questions.questionHtml:
Which scheme among the following is most beneficial to the customer?

(i) Successive discounts of 25% and 25%
(ii) Flat discount of 40%
(iii) Buy one, get one free
(iv) Successive discounts of 30% and 20%
questions.solution:
Explanation:

Let the marked price = ₹100

(i) 25% and 25% successive discount
= 100 × 0.75 × 0.75 = ₹56.25
Discount = 43.75%

(ii) Flat 40% discount
= ₹60
Discount = 40%

(iii) Buy 1 Get 1 Free
Pay ₹100 for 2 items → ₹50 each
Discount = 50%

(iv) 30% and 20% successive discount
= 100 × 0.7 × 0.8 = ₹56
Discount = 44%

👉 The highest discount = Highest discount = 50% (Buy 1 Get 1 Free)

questions.question: A shopkeeper has 3 different qualities of oil — 725 litres of 1st quality, 783 litres of 2nd quality, and 812 litres of 3rd quality. Find the least possible number of bottles of equal size in which different oils of different qualities can be filled without mixing.
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper has 3 different qualities of oil — 725 litres of 1st quality, 783 litres of 2nd quality, and 812 litres of 3rd quality. Find the least possible number of bottles of equal size in which different oils of different qualities can be filled without mixing.
questions.solution:
To find the least number of bottles,
we need to find the HCF (Highest Common Factor) of 725, 783, and 812.
This gives the maximum size of each bottle.

HCF(725, 783, 812) = 29

Now,
Number of bottles = (725 ÷ 29) + (783 ÷ 29) + (812 ÷ 29)
= 25 + 27 + 28
= 80

questions.question: Lakshmi and Faiz started a car race from the same point, in the same direction and at the same circular track of length 1725 m with speeds of 72 km/h and 90 km/h respectively. After how much time (in seconds) will they meet again for the first time?
questions.questionHtml: Lakshmi and Faiz started a car race from the same point, in the same direction and at the same circular track of length 1725 m with speeds of 72 km/h and 90 km/h respectively. After how much time (in seconds) will they meet again for the first time?
questions.solution:
Relative speed = (90 − 72) km/h = 18 km/h
= (18 × 1000) / 3600 = 5 m/s

Time = Distance / Relative speed
= 1725 / 5 = 345 seconds

questions.question: Meena, Archana and Geeta alone can complete a work in 6 hours, 9 hours and 18 hours respectively. If they work together, how much time will they take to complete half the work?
questions.questionHtml: Meena, Archana and Geeta alone can complete a work in 6 hours, 9 hours and 18 hours respectively. If they work together, how much time will they take to complete half the work?
questions.solution:
Meena = 6

Archana= 9

Geeta = 18

So, their 1-hour works are in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1 (taking LCM = 18)

∴ T = ½ * 18 / (3 + 2 + 1)
= 9 / 6
= 1.5 hours

questions.question: In a right-angled triangle ABC, if ∠ABC = 90°, AB = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm, and BD is perpendicular to AC, then what is the value of AD : DC?
questions.questionHtml: In a right-angled triangle ABC, if ∠ABC = 90°, AB = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm, and BD is perpendicular to AC, then what is the value of AD : DC?
questions.solution:
In right-angled triangle ABC,
AC² = AB² + BC²
= 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100
⟹ AC = 10 cm

Now, when BD ⟂ AC,
AD/DC = (AB²) / (BC²)

So,
AD : DC = 6² : 8² = 36 : 64 = 9 : 16

questions.question: What is the difference (in Rs.) between the interests on Rs. 30,000 for one year at 8% per annum compounded half-yearly and yearly?
questions.questionHtml: What is the difference (in Rs.) between the interests on Rs. 30,000 for one year at 8% per annum compounded half-yearly and yearly?
questions.solution:
Given:
P = 30,000 R = 8% T = 1 yr

Yearly CI rate: 8%
Half-yearly CI rate: Half-yearly rate = 4% per half year

So, for one year:
= 4% + 4% + (4×4)/100
= 8% + 0.16%
= 8.16%

Difference in rate = 8.16 − 8 = 0.16%

Difference = (0.16/100) × 30,000 = ₹48

questions.question: The average of nine consecutive positive integers is d. If the last two numbers are excluded, by how much will the average increase or decrease?
questions.questionHtml: The average of nine consecutive positive integers is d. If the last two numbers are excluded, by how much will the average increase or decrease?
questions.solution:
Explanation:

Let the numbers be:
x, x+1, x+2, … , x+10

Average = (x + x+10) / 2 = x + 5 = d

If the last two numbers (x+9, x+10) are excluded,
remaining numbers = 9 numbers (x to x+8)

New average = (x + x+8) / 2 = x + 4

Decrease in average = (x + 5) − (x + 4) = 1
